title: Existing nodes each need one recycle to gain the drift-hash annotations

detection.reason: the annotations sit on Machine and Provisioner objects (the v1alpha5 API), which this platform does not collect

quote: Karpenter will now statically drift on both Provisioner and AWSNodeTemplate Fields. For Provisioner Static Drift, the `karpenter.sh/provisioner-hash` annotation must be present on both the Provisioner and Machine. For AWSNodeTemplate drift, the `karpenter.k8s.aws/nodetemplate-hash` annotation must be present on the AWSNodeTemplate and Machine. Karpenter will not add these annotations to pre-existing nodes, so each of these nodes will need to be recycled one time for the annotations to be added.
remediation: Expect every pre-existing node to be replaced once after this upgrade. Karpenter does not backfill the `karpenter.sh/provisioner-hash` and `karpenter.k8s.aws/nodetemplate-hash` annotations, so each node has to cycle through once before static drift works for it.

title: A node template mixing id selectors with other selectors stops validating

detection.reason: AWSNodeTemplate and Provisioner spec.provider are the v1alpha5 alpha API, which this platform does not collect

quote: Karpenter will now fail validation on AWSNodeTemplates and Provisioner `spec.provider` that have `amiSelectors`, `subnetSelectors`, or `securityGroupSelectors` set with a combination of id selectors (`aws-ids`, `aws::ids`) and other selectors.
remediation: Split any `amiSelector`, `subnetSelector` or `securityGroupSelector` that combines an id selector (`aws-ids`, `aws::ids`) with another selector into separate selectors. Once validation starts rejecting the combination, edits to that object fail.
verifyCommand: kubectl get awsnodetemplates,provisioners -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each object printed uses the alpha API and needs its selectors checked by hand

title: Karpenter's securityContext can no longer be overridden through Helm

detection.reason: the rendered workload shows the securityContext in force, not whether your Helm values tried to set a different one

quote: Karpenter now statically sets the `securityContext` at both the pod and container-levels and doesn't allow override values to be passed through the Helm chart. This change was made to adhere to Restricted Pod Security Standard, which follows pod hardening best practices.
remediation: If you override Karpenter's pod or container `securityContext` through Helm values, those overrides stop taking effect. Sidecars that cannot run under the Restricted Pod Security Standard need their own securityContext set in the deployment instead.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("karpenter/controller")) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)"'  # the Karpenter controller workload and the exact version tag it runs -- then read the pod and container securityContext
